issues.display_title: Issue #513: Parallel Chunk Download for UploadPanorama Worker
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Parallel Chunk Download for UploadPanorama Worker

Changes

  • Created DownloadFileParallel in src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/parallel_download.go providing multi-connection chunked downloading via HTTP Range: bytes=start-end.
  • Replaced os/exec curl command in src/Worker/UploadPanorama/UploadPanorama.go with PostFunctions.DownloadFileParallel.
  • Implemented custom http.Transport with dynamic DialContext routing to support serverIp target routing and InsecureSkipVerify TLS (replacing curl's --resolve and -k).
  • Implemented file probing (HEAD + GET Range: bytes=0-0) with graceful zero-waste fallback to single-stream downloading when Range is unsupported or file is small (< 2 MB).
  • Implemented concurrent non-overlapping chunk writes using os.File.WriteAt after pre-allocating the file via Truncate.
  • Added per-chunk retry logic (up to 3 attempts) with byte offset resumption and exponential backoff.
  • Added background progress reporter logging download progress (percent, MB, and MB/s) every 3 seconds.
  • Added support for UPLOAD_DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY environment variable (default: 8 connections).
  • Added comprehensive unit tests in src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/parallel_download_test.go.

Files

  • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/parallel_download.go
  • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/parallel_download_test.go
  • src/Worker/UploadPanorama/UploadPanorama.go

Verification

go test -v -run TestDownloadFileParallel ./src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/...
go test ./src/...
go build ./src/Worker/UploadPanorama/UploadPanorama.go

Results:

  • TestDownloadFileParallel_RangeSuccess: PASS (5 MB test file downloaded across 4 parallel chunks; byte verification passed).
  • TestDownloadFileParallel_NoRangeFallback: PASS (non-range server handled gracefully via single-stream fallback).
  • TestDownloadFileParallel_ServerError: PASS (HTTP 404 handled cleanly and incomplete files pruned).
  • TestDownloadFileParallel_ResolveServerIp: PASS (custom server IP and host header routing verified).
  • TestDownloadFileParallel_ResolveServerIp_RangeSuccess: PASS (custom server IP combined with chunked range requests).
  • All existing repository packages pass tests.
  • Worker binary builds cleanly without compile or type errors.

Git

  • Implemented in branch development.

Problem

When the UploadPanorama worker downloads panorama files from the source web server (serverIp), it executes single-connection curl with --resolve and -k.

Web servers often apply per-connection bandwidth throttling (e.g., ~200–296 KB/s). For large panoramas (such as 94 MB), this single-stream download takes over 5 minutes and 26 seconds, creating a significant processing bottleneck before files can be stored in S3/MinIO and recorded in the database.

Scope

  • Replace the external curl process in src/Worker/UploadPanorama/UploadPanorama.go with a native Go parallel chunk downloader.
  • Use HTTP Range: bytes=start-end to download multiple non-overlapping segments concurrently across multiple TCP connections.
  • Preserve custom host resolution and insecure TLS handling equivalent to curl's --resolve and -k.
  • Fall back to standard single-connection streaming if the target server does not support Range requests or if the file is smaller than 2 MB.
  • Write chunks directly and concurrently to disk using os.File.WriteAt.
  • Provide per-chunk retries (up to 3 times) with offset resumption.
  • Allow concurrency configuration via the environment variable UPLOAD_DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY (default: 8).
  • Provide periodic console progress logs (downloaded MB, percent, MB/s).

Behavior Boundary

  • The RabbitMQ message payload format, queue names, and acknowledgment semantics remain unchanged.
  • Output file path and temporary file removal after MinIO upload remain unchanged.
  • S3/MinIO upload logic, database queries, and Redis status updates remain identical.
  • The downloader behaves transparently: errors during download trigger existing error logging (SaveLogErr) and exit flow.

Out of Scope

  • Changing the PHP upstream file-handling or RabbitMQ dispatch format.
  • Modifying S3 bucket or MinIO upload mechanisms.
  • Changing multiple_post or posts table schemas.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A 94 MB file download utilizes multiple parallel connections, overcoming per-connection bandwidth caps.
  • Output file matches the source file byte-for-byte.
  • Server without Range support falls back to single-stream download without failing.
  • Network hiccups on individual chunks recover via retry loop.
  • All unit tests pass and code compiles without errors.

Delivery

Implemented on 2026-09-24.

issues.display_title: Issue #515: Event-Driven Add Post Complete (Eliminate Race Condition)
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Event-Driven Add Post Complete (Eliminate Race Condition)

Architecture Change

Before (Polling)

Client --> /v1/posts/complete --> RabbitMQ(_add_post_complete) --> PostComplete worker
                                                                      |
                                                                      v
                                                              Poll Redis every 5s
                                                              (max 100x = ~8.3 min)
                                                                      |
                                                            +---------+---------+
                                                            |                   |
                                                       All ready?          Limit reached?
                                                            |                   |
                                                       Process post      Delete post + notify

After (Event-Driven)

Client --> /v1/posts/complete --> Save payload to Redis
                                  |
                                  +--> All files already ready? (edge case)
                                       YES --> TryAcquirePostCompleteTrigger (SETNX)
                                               --> Publish to RabbitMQ
                                       NO  --> Wait for UploadPanorama worker

UploadPanorama worker (per file):
    Set Redis status = "success"
        |
        v
    CheckAllPanoramaReady? AND Payload exists?
        |
        YES --> TryAcquirePostCompleteTrigger (SETNX)
                --> Only ONE winner publishes to RabbitMQ(_add_post_complete)
        NO  --> Skip (more files pending or client hasn't hit /complete yet)

PostComplete worker:
    Consume message --> Process directly (all files guaranteed ready)
    No polling, no sleep, no requeue.

Changes

1. src/Utils/Redis/panorama_cache.go -- New Redis Functions

Added 6 new functions and TTL constants:

  • SavePostCompletePayload(sid, payload) -- Stores the base64-encoded payload from /v1/posts/complete with 24h TTL. Key: {prefix}_post_complete_payload:{sid}.
  • GetPostCompletePayload(sid) -- Retrieves the stored payload.
  • DeletePostCompletePayload(sid) -- Removes the payload after successful processing.
  • CheckAllPanoramaReady(sid) -- Uses SCAN + MGET to check if all panorama status keys for a SID have value "success". Returns (allReady bool, totalFiles int).
  • TryAcquirePostCompleteTrigger(sid) -- Uses SETNX to atomically claim the right to trigger PostComplete. Only the first caller gets true. Key: {prefix}_post_complete_trigger_lock:{sid}.
  • DeletePostCompleteTriggerLock(sid) -- Cleans up the trigger lock after processing.

Added TTL to existing function:

  • SetPanoramaStatus() -- Changed from TTL=0 (no expiry) to TTL=24h to prevent orphaned keys.

2. src/Controllers/V1/Posts/PostsHandlers.go -- Modified Handler

AddPostCompleteV1 changes:

  • DB update moved before Redis/RabbitMQ operations -- is_uploading=false, is_processing=true is now set first, preventing the "publish before DB update" crash window.
  • Payload saved to Redis instead of publishing directly to RabbitMQ. The UploadPanorama worker will retrieve this payload and trigger PostComplete when ready.
  • Edge case check -- After saving the payload, immediately checks CheckAllPanoramaReady. If all files are already uploaded (small files finish before client hits /complete), triggers PostComplete via TryAcquirePostCompleteTrigger + RabbitMQ.Publish.
  • Fixed incorrect comment // UPLOAD PANORAMA POST V1 to // ADD POST COMPLETE V1.

3. src/Worker/UploadPanorama/UploadPanorama.go -- Event-Driven Trigger

After setting Redis.SetPanoramaStatus(slug, uName, "success"), added:

  • Check CheckAllPanoramaReady(slug) -- are all files for this SID now "success"?
  • Check GetPostCompletePayload(slug) -- has the client submitted the complete payload?
  • If both conditions met: TryAcquirePostCompleteTrigger(slug) -- atomic SETNX lock.
    • Winner: publishes payload to _add_post_complete queue.
    • Loser: logs skip message (another worker already triggered it).
    • On publish failure: releases the lock via DeletePostCompleteTriggerLock so it can be retried.

4. src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go -- Removed Polling

Removed:

  • Entire polling/requeue loop (Redis status checking, time.Sleep(5s), delivery.Reject(true), requeue counter logic).
  • sendPostFailure() function (was called when requeue limit reached -- no longer applicable).
  • CheckAndSetPanoramaStatus() function (filesystem fallback check -- no longer needed).

Changed:

  • Consumer now processes messages directly without any readiness checks.
  • Redis panorama cleanup moved outside if elastic {} block so both publish and draft paths clean up their keys.
  • Added DeletePostCompletePayload(sid) and DeletePostCompleteTriggerLock(sid) at the end of the success path.
  • Removed duplicate DeleteRequeueStatus call (was called both inside if elastic {} and outside).

Race Condition Prevention

The TryAcquirePostCompleteTrigger function uses Redis SETNX (Set if Not eXists), which is an atomic operation. This guarantees:

Scenario Result
Two UploadPanorama workers finish simultaneously Only one SETNX returns true, only one publishes
/v1/posts/complete handler and UploadPanorama worker race Only one SETNX returns true, only one publishes
Single UploadPanorama worker finishes last SETNX returns true, it publishes
/v1/posts/complete arrives after all files uploaded SETNX returns true, handler publishes immediately

Backward Compatibility

All existing APK versions continue to work without changes:

  • API contract unchanged -- /v1/posts/upload and /v1/posts/complete accept the same request format and return the same response format and status codes.
  • No new required fields -- Payloads from old APK versions are fully compatible.
  • Changes are internal only -- The switch from "publish to RabbitMQ directly" to "save to Redis, let UploadPanorama trigger" is invisible to the client.

Redis Keys Overview

Key Pattern Set By Read By Deleted By TTL
{prefix}_panorama_status:{sid}:{fileName} RegisterPanoramaName ("pending"), UploadPanorama ("success") CheckAllPanoramaReady PostComplete worker 24h
{prefix}_post_complete_payload:{sid} /v1/posts/complete handler UploadPanorama worker PostComplete worker 24h
{prefix}_post_complete_trigger_lock:{sid} TryAcquirePostCompleteTrigger (SETNX) -- PostComplete worker 24h

Files

  • src/Utils/Redis/panorama_cache.go
  • src/Controllers/V1/Posts/PostsHandlers.go
  • src/Worker/UploadPanorama/UploadPanorama.go
  • src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go

Verification

go build ./src/Worker/UploadPanorama/UploadPanorama.go
go build ./src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go
go build ./...

Manual test scenarios:

  1. Normal flow -- Upload 3 panorama files (small), then hit /v1/posts/complete. PostComplete should trigger and complete.
  2. Large file -- Upload 1 panorama file (94 MB). Hit /v1/posts/complete while upload is still in progress. PostComplete should trigger only after upload finishes, regardless of how long it takes.
  3. Edge case -- Upload all files first (very fast), then hit /v1/posts/complete. Handler should detect all files ready and trigger PostComplete immediately.
  4. Draft flow -- Same as above but with action=draft. Redis keys should be cleaned up after completion.

Git

  • Implemented in branch development.

Problem

The Add Post flow has a race condition between the UploadPanorama worker and the PostComplete worker. When a client calls /v1/posts/complete, the handler immediately publishes a message to the _add_post_complete RabbitMQ queue. The PostComplete worker then polls Redis every 5 seconds (up to 100 times) to check whether all panorama files have finished uploading.

This polling approach causes several failures:

  1. Timeout on large files -- 100 retries x 5 seconds = ~8.3 minutes maximum wait. A 94 MB panorama file can take 15+ minutes to download from the source server and upload to S3, exceeding the retry limit. When the limit is reached, the worker deletes the post and sends a failure notification to the user.

  2. Blocking consumer -- time.Sleep(5 * time.Second) inside the RabbitMQ consumer callback blocks the goroutine. If there is only one consumer and multiple posts are being processed, they queue up behind the sleep.

  3. Double ack/reject bug -- defer delivery.Ack(false) on line 167 conflicts with delivery.Reject(true) on line 254. After Reject returns, the deferred Ack still fires. RabbitMQ silently ignores the second call, but this is fragile and semantically incorrect.

  4. Publish before DB update -- The handler publishes to RabbitMQ first (line 214), then updates the database (line 219). If the API crashes between these two operations, the message is in the queue but the post is still is_processing=false, causing the worker to fail with "No post found."

  5. Wasted resources -- The worker repeatedly wakes, queries Redis, sleeps, rejects, and re-consumes the same message dozens of times for a single post.

Scope

  • Replace the polling/requeue mechanism in PostComplete worker with an event-driven trigger from the UploadPanorama worker.
  • The /v1/posts/complete handler saves the payload to Redis instead of publishing directly to RabbitMQ.
  • The UploadPanorama worker, after each file upload completes, checks whether ALL files for that SID are ready and whether the client has submitted the complete payload. If both conditions are met, it publishes to the _add_post_complete queue.
  • Use Redis SETNX (atomic set-if-not-exists) to guarantee exactly one actor triggers the PostComplete worker, preventing duplicate processing.
  • Add 24-hour TTL to all Redis keys involved in the flow for automatic cleanup of abandoned posts.
  • Move Redis panorama status cleanup outside the if elastic {} (publish-only) block so draft posts also clean up their keys.

Behavior Boundary

  • The HTTP API contract (request format, response format, status codes) for /v1/posts/upload and /v1/posts/complete remains identical. No client-side changes required.
  • The RabbitMQ queue names (_upload_panorama, _add_post_complete) remain unchanged.
  • The PostComplete worker's processing logic (DB updates, Elasticsearch indexing, push notifications, Centrifugo websocket, Maps Panorra sync) remains unchanged.
  • The RegisterPanoramaName endpoint behavior remains unchanged.
  • APK versions that use the old flow (/v1/posts/complete and /v1/posts/upload) continue to work without any client-side update.

Out of Scope

  • Changing the PHP upstream (upload_panorra.php) file handling or RabbitMQ dispatch format.
  • Modifying the synchronous (non-V1) Add Post flow (/posts/upload-panorama, /posts/complete).
  • Adding idempotency keys to endpoints.
  • Refactoring the 900+ line PostComplete.go into smaller functions.
  • Adding structured logging to replace fmt.Println.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A 94 MB panorama file upload completes successfully regardless of how long the upload takes (no 8.3-minute timeout).
  • The PostComplete worker only receives messages when all panorama files are guaranteed uploaded.
  • No duplicate PostComplete processing occurs, even when multiple UploadPanorama workers finish simultaneously.
  • No duplicate processing when /v1/posts/complete and the last UploadPanorama worker race.
  • Draft posts correctly clean up Redis panorama status keys.
  • Redis keys are automatically cleaned up within 24 hours if the flow is abandoned.
  • All existing APK versions continue to work without changes.

Delivery

Implemented on 2026-09-24.
